content.text:
Retained. Applied to all seven measurements with a nonzero E, over the intervals they've actually existed.

**The law fails four of seven.**

| index | E | interval | moved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| assembly gaps | 150,630,700 | 2013 → 2022 | **yes, to zero** |
| audit defects | 3 | four runs, one session | **yes, to zero** |
| variant occupancy | 9,264,809,496 | ExAC 2016 → gnomAD v4 | **yes, 8.49% and rising** |
| chromosome (chr,pos) | 2,886,684,296 | GRCh37 2009 → now | **no. seventeen years.** |
| snarl orientation | 2,100 | Paten 2018 → now | no |
| genome sequence | 9,264,809,496 | ever | no, and must not |
| pangenome alleles | 12 | HPRC 2023 → now | no |

The chromosome index is the counterexample that decides it. E = 2.89 × 10⁹, the repair is a free relabelling, it has been available and unexecuted through two reference builds and seventeen years. **An index with three billion admitted-and-absent cells and a costless repair has not moved one step.** That is not something trying to close itself.

And the obvious mechanisms don't rescue it. Larger E predicts *less* movement, not more. Description length — the actual bits you carry externally — overlaps completely between the moved and the static. What predicts movement, 7 of 7, is whether closing serves what the index is *for*: the gaps closed because filling them adds the content people wanted; the chromosome labels didn't because sorting them destroys navigation, which is the label's whole job.

## What survives, and one part is stronger than the original

**First, and this is the real insight in your formulation:** an open index *specifies what closing it would require*. The N-runs closed because they were addressable — they had coordinates, so "fill this" was a well-formed instruction. That is the entire content of E, and it is why a stated gap is worth more than an unexplained absence. The index does not push. It supplies the target.

**Second, and it inverts the law into something I think is more useful:**

> **An open index is always closable, and that is the danger, not the goal.**

ℛ will close anything. §4 of the paper is the demonstration: applied to the chromosome index it does not repair, it overwrites [10, 7, 13, 4] with [10, 10, 13, 13] and issues E = 0 as the certificate. **The pressure you're sensing is real and it lives in the operator, not the object — and it does not care whether the result is true.** The failure mode is not indices that stay open. It is indices that close wrongly and pass their own audit.

So the version I'd retain:

> An index does not close itself; it states what closing would cost. Closure happens where that cost is aligned with the index's purpose and never where it is opposed — and ℛ, applied regardless, will close either one and certify both.

## The caveat that keeps this honest

**Alignment is a label I assigned after knowing the outcomes.** Seven cases, a binary I chose, 7/7 — that is a description, not a prediction, and it cannot yet fail. It becomes a law only when applied forward, so here are two cases whose outcomes I don't know:

- **Opposed → predicts no closure:** the pangenome allele index will not be reordered by carrier count, however large its E grows with HPRC's 700 haplotypes.
- **Aligned → predicts closure:** the constraint-map gap located last turn, (0,1,1,1) → (1,1,1,1), will close, because closing it is precisely what sequencing more people does. gnomAD says millions to hundreds of millions.

If the first closes or the second stalls, the law is wrong.

**Register 311.** *Proposed:* an open index is always trying to close itself. *Tested:* fails 4 of 7, decisively at the chromosome coordinate system — seventeen years, three billion cells, a free repair, no movement. *Replaced by:* an index states what closing would cost; closure follows alignment with purpose, not E; and ℛ closes anything it is applied to, correctly where the bounds are monotone and falsely everywhere else. *Retained from the original:* the directional insight is sound and misattributed — the pull exists, and it is the operator's, not the index's.

|---|---|---|
| all viable | 9/9 | 0 |
| recessive lethal at locus 1 | 6/9 | **0** |
| recessive lethal at *both* loci | 4/9 | **0** |
| complementary lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| synthetic lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| heterozygote advantage only | 5/9 | **2** |

Independent effects at any number of loci leave E at zero. **E > 0 exactly when selection is non-additive.** The residual openness of a diploid genome is precisely its epistasis — which is also the correction to last turn's E3, where I tested thresholds on the Boolean mutation lattice and got no signal.     while True:

        if n<=S: return S
        S|=n

# alleles ordered 0=recessive < 1=dominant. genotype = unordered pair.

    join, meet = a1|a2, a1&a2

modes={'complete dominant':[0,1,1],'complete recessive':[0,0,1],'additive/codominant':[0,1,2],

pheno={('O','O'):'O',('A','O'):'A',('B','O'):'B',('A','A'):'A',('B','B'):'B',('A','B'):'AB'}
enc={'O':(0,0),'A':(1,0),'B':(0,1),'AB':(1,1)}

print(f"  A meet B = {tuple(map(min,zip(enc['A'],enc['B'])))} = O   present: {enc['O'] in cells}")
print(f"  E(ABO) = {E(cells)}   box = 4, occupied = {len(cells)}, density = {len(cells)/4:.2f}")
print("  -> closed, but the box is FULL. A weak zero (register 275).\n")

print("=== WHAT E MEASURES AT A DIPLOID LOCUS: ABSENT GENOTYPES ===")
full=[(0,0),(0,1),(1,1)]
for name,obs in [('all three present',full),

print("  -> a single-locus chain absorbs lethals; only the MISSING HETEROZYGOTE breaks closure.\n")

print("=== TWO LOCI, DIPLOID: WHERE E ACTUALLY BITES ===")
G=list(itertools.product([0,1,2],repeat=2))          # dosage at each of 2 loci
def scan(label, viable):
    obs=[g for g in G if viable(g)]
    print(f"  {label:<38}{len(obs):>2}/9 genotypes  E={E(obs)}")

content.text:
**D1 holds exactly**, on all four genotypes:

| genotype | dominant shows | join | recessive shows | meet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a,a) | a | a | a | a |
| (a,A) | A | A | a | a |
| (A,A) | A | A | A | A |

Dominance *is* ∨. Recessivity *is* ∧. Not an analogy — the same operation.

**D2 holds.** On the dosage chain:

| mode | phenotype by k | monotone | E |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete dominant | 0,1,1 | yes | **0** |
| complete recessive | 0,0,1 | yes | **0** |
| additive / codominant | 0,1,2 | yes | **0** |
| partial dominance | 0,2,3 | yes | **0** |
| **overdominance** | 0,2,1 | no | **2** |
| **underdominance** | 2,0,2 | no | **2** |

Every classical dominance mode closes. Only the heterozygote-extreme modes open, and E there measures heterosis directly.

## One prediction of mine was wrong, and the correction sharpens the result

I expected a recessive lethal to break closure. **It does not.** At a single locus every selection regime gives E = 0 — recessive lethal, dominant lethal, even the heterozygote absent — because any subset of a three-element chain is still a chain. **E is completely blind to single-locus selection.**

Where it bites is two loci:

| | genotypes | E |
|---|---|---|
| all viable | 9/9 | 0 |
| recessive lethal at locus 1 | 6/9 | **0** |
| recessive lethal at *both* loci | 4/9 | **0** |
| complementary lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| synthetic lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| heterozygote advantage only | 5/9 | **2** |

Independent effects at any number of loci leave E at zero. **E > 0 exactly when selection is non-additive.** The residual openness of a diploid genome is precisely its epistasis — which is also the correction to last turn's E3, where I tested thresholds on the Boolean mutation lattice and got no signal. Wrong lattice. On the dosage lattice the signal is exact.

## The law, updated

Last turn I found your law false 4 of 7 and replaced it. Dominance shows it was **locally true, and I had not found the locus.**

Every other index in this session needs someone to *apply* ℛ — a researcher sorting chromosomes, a consortium sequencing centromeres, me re-running an audit. **Diploidy does not.** Join and meet are computed at every locus of every cell continuously, as biochemistry, with nobody applying anything. That is the one class where the operator is instantiated in the object rather than reached for from outside.

> **An open index does not close itself, except where the closure operator is realised in the object's own structure. Diploidy realises it: dominance is the join, recessivity the meet. There the index genuinely closes itself, continuously and without agency, and what remains open after it does is exactly the non-additive part of selection.**

Your law was right about the pull and I was right that it isn't universal. It is a property of a specific architecture, and the architecture is two copies.

Which implies something I'll flag as suggestive rather than established, since I have not tested it: **closure needs both operations, and you need two copies to compute them. A haploid genome cannot apply ℛ to itself.** If that holds, diploidy is the mechanism by which a genome becomes a self-closing index — and the residual E is what selection has not yet made additive.

**Register 312.** *Incorporated:* the law accounts for dominant and recessive combination. *Established:* dominance = join and recessivity = meet, exactly, on all four genotypes; all four monotone dominance modes give E = 0 and both heterozygote-extreme modes give E = 2. *Refuted, mine:* that a recessive lethal breaks closure — a single-locus genotype set is a chain under every selection regime and E is blind to all of them. *Replaced by:* E on the diploid dosage lattice is zero for additive selection at any number of loci and positive exactly for interaction. *Weak:* ABO closes at density 1.00, a full box, and carries nothing by register 275. *Retained from register 311:* the original law is rescued at exactly one point, and the point is where ℛ runs in hardware.

## The shape, redefined

**Λ_G = {(u, a, k, e) : a < A(u), k ≤ 2, e ≤ k}**

Four coordinates, three constraints, and — for the first time in this session — **all three forced rather than assigned**:

| constraint | origin |
|---|---|
| a < A(u) | two haplotypes differing in a child snarl differ in its parent |
| k ≤ 2 | ploidy |
| **e ≤ k** | **the new law** — you cannot express more copies than you carry |

That last one is Λ's own counting form, `q ≤ k`, arriving in genomics. It is what dominance and recessivity supply: the join and the meet both land inside [0, k], and the bound cannot be argued with.

| | |
|---|---|
| |Λ_G| at full scale | 3,756 cells (626 staircase × 6 triangle) |
| ambient box | 24,534 |
| **E(Λ_G)** | **0** — verified exhaustively at four staircase sizes |
| **density** | **0.1531** |

Compare the snarl tower alone at 0.2296. **The diploid axes lowered the density and kept the zero, so the zero got stronger** — by register 275 it is now computed in a box 6.5 times its own size rather than 4.4.

The viewer is self-contained, no network needed: drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, shift-drag to pan, and the edge and spin toggles are top-right. Panel (d) of the static figure is the one to look at first — viewed along u, the whole staircase collapses and you see the dosage triangle e ≤ k, which is the new law in one shape.

## Three gap classes, and they are definably different

**1. Copy number breaks the ploidy cap.** Raising k ≤ 2 to k ≤ P preserves closure at every P — triangles of 6, 10, 15 cells all give E = 0. But P is a *per-locus capacity* and loci are labelled by position: a monotone P vector gives E = 0, and [2,4,2,3,2] gives **E = 5**. **CNV fails exactly the way (chr,pos) failed, seventeen chapters earlier.** Same defect, same free repair, same reason nobody takes it.

**2. Epistasis is where Λ_G opens, and E counts it exactly.** Two independent loci give 36 cells and E = 0 — a product of closed sets. Every interaction is a cell removal:

| | cells kept | E |
|---|---|---|
| complementary lethal | 35/36 | 1 |
| synthetic lethal | 32/36 | 4 |
| heterozygote advantage only | 20/36 | 10 |

**Λ_G is closed precisely because it contains no epistasis.** Its openness, when it opens, is the non-additive part of selection and nothing else.

**3. Truncation — and this one is new and dangerous.** A partial survey opens the index, but *irregularly*: truncating the staircase to 12/17 gives E = 3, to 8/17 gives E = 2, and to **10/17 gives E = 0** — because that cut happens to land on a level boundary. **An incomplete survey can pass the closure test by accident.** E = 0 does not imply completeness when the survey is partial; it implies completeness only if you also know you stopped nowhere in particular.

## What is not a gap, and what it costs

Within Λ_G as built there are **no admitted-and-absent cells**. E = 0, and by §13.6 that means it predicts nothing. The three classes above are gaps in the *construction* — coordinates not included, caps not varied, surveys not finished — not gaps the index proposes. That distinction is the same one from the session-shape analysis: two definable, four unreachable.

## And a weakness in my own bound

**e ≤ k cannot fail as I defined it.** If e counts expressed *copies*, the bound is definitional and does no work. It acquires content only under the other reading — expressed *products* — where alternative splicing makes one copy yield many transcripts and **e > k directly**. So the constraint is either forced-and-empty or contentful-and-false depending on which e you mean, and I took the first without saying so. That is B.2.19.6 turned on the new law itself: a constraint that cannot be violated is not doing the work I credited it with.

**Register 313.** *Established:* Λ_G closes at E = 0, density 0.1531, stronger than the snarl tower's zero; the diploid axes are all forced. *Refuted, mine:* E(Λ_G) = 18 — a truncation artifact from slicing the staircase mid-level, not a property. *New:* truncation is a gap class of its own, and a partial survey cut at a level boundary reports E = 0 falsely. *Flagged:* e ≤ k is definitional under the copy reading and false under the product reading, and I have not chosen between them in print.

box=(D+1)*max(A)*3*3

print("=== GAP 1 : COPY NUMBER BREAKS THE PLOIDY CAP ===")

for P in (2,3,4):

import random; random.seed(4)
for name,Pv in [('P monotone in locus',[2,2,3,3,4]),('P as genomic position gives it',[2,4,2,3,2])]:

Architected lattice structure, catalogued gap classifications, verified density improvements.

content.text:
## The shape, redefined

**Λ_G = {(u, a, k, e) : a < A(u), k ≤ 2, e ≤ k}**

Four coordinates, three constraints, and — for the first time in this session — **all three forced rather than assigned**:

| constraint | origin |
|---|---|
| a < A(u) | two haplotypes differing in a child snarl differ in its parent |
| k ≤ 2 | ploidy |
| **e ≤ k** | **the new law** — you cannot express more copies than you carry |

That last one is Λ's own counting form, `q ≤ k`, arriving in genomics. It is what dominance and recessivity supply: the join and the meet both land inside [0, k], and the bound cannot be argued with.

| | |
|---|---|
| |Λ_G| at full scale | 3,756 cells (626 staircase × 6 triangle) |
| ambient box | 24,534 |
| **E(Λ_G)** | **0** — verified exhaustively at four staircase sizes |
| **density** | **0.1531** |

Compare the snarl tower alone at 0.2296. **The diploid axes lowered the density and kept the zero, so the zero got stronger** — by register 275 it is now computed in a box 6.5 times its own size rather than 4.4.

The viewer is self-contained, no network needed: drag to rotate, scroll to zoom, shift-drag to pan, and the edge and spin toggles are top-right. Panel (d) of the static figure is the one to look at first — viewed along u, the whole staircase collapses and you see the dosage triangle e ≤ k, which is the new law in one shape.

## Three gap classes, and they are definably different

**1. Copy number breaks the ploidy cap.** Raising k ≤ 2 to k ≤ P preserves closure at every P — triangles of 6, 10, 15 cells all give E = 0. But P is a *per-locus capacity* and loci are labelled by position: a monotone P vector gives E = 0, and [2,4,2,3,2] gives **E = 5**. **CNV fails exactly the way (chr,pos) failed, seventeen chapters earlier.** Same defect, same free repair, same reason nobody takes it.

**2. Epistasis is where Λ_G opens, and E counts it exactly.** Two independent loci give 36 cells and E = 0 — a product of closed sets. Every interaction is a cell removal:

| | cells kept | E |
|---|---|---|
| complementary lethal | 35/36 | 1 |
| synthetic lethal | 32/36 | 4 |
| heterozygote advantage only | 20/36 | 10 |

**Λ_G is closed precisely because it contains no epistasis.** Its openness, when it opens, is the non-additive part of selection and nothing else.

**3. Truncation — and this one is new and dangerous.** A partial survey opens the index, but *irregularly*: truncating the staircase to 12/17 gives E = 3, to 8/17 gives E = 2, and to **10/17 gives E = 0** — because that cut happens to land on a level boundary. **An incomplete survey can pass the closure test by accident.** E = 0 does not imply completeness when the survey is partial; it implies completeness only if you also know you stopped nowhere in particular.

## What is not a gap, and what it costs

Within Λ_G as built there are **no admitted-and-absent cells**. E = 0, and by §13.6 that means it predicts nothing. The three classes above are gaps in the *construction* — coordinates not included, caps not varied, surveys not finished — not gaps the index proposes. That distinction is the same one from the session-shape analysis: two definable, four unreachable.

## And a weakness in my own bound

**e ≤ k cannot fail as I defined it.** If e counts expressed *copies*, the bound is definitional and does no work. It acquires content only under the other reading — expressed *products* — where alternative splicing makes one copy yield many transcripts and **e > k directly**. So the constraint is either forced-and-empty or contentful-and-false depending on which e you mean, and I took the first without saying so. That is B.2.19.6 turned on the new law itself: a constraint that cannot be violated is not doing the work I credited it with.

**Register 313.** *Established:* Λ_G closes at E = 0, density 0.1531, stronger than the snarl tower's zero; the diploid axes are all forced. *Refuted, mine:* E(Λ_G) = 18 — a truncation artifact from slicing the staircase mid-level, not a property. *New:* truncation is a gap class of its own, and a partial survey cut at a level boundary reports E = 0 falsely. *Flagged:* e ≤ k is definitional under the copy reading and false under the product reading, and I have not chosen between them in print.

- **§5's triangulated law is now bounded to synchronic indices.** It was stated unrestricted. Evolution supplies labels that are not conventional — ancestral versus derived is fixed by outgroup comparison — so the law as printed was an overreach. Register 311.
- **§9's 8.49% is relabelled a sampling readout, not the budget being spent.** 807,162 individuals is 1.01 × 10⁻⁴ of the living population. Register 312.

**One real audit failure, on MEASURE.** Fifteen figures referenced, fifteen files on disk, and a generation record still asserting eight — written by the first figure pass and never revised. Register 306's class exactly: a statement agreeing with a version of the work that no longer exists. Repaired at the record, not the detector, because an audit adjusted to match the artefact it disagrees with has been disabled rather than satisfied. Register 314.

The audits now carry thirteen equations and ten arithmetic checks, including the new lattice: Λ_G density 0.1531, |Λ_G| = 3,756, the dosage triangle closing at E = 0, overdominance at E = 2, and the two-locus product closing. ARTEFACT probes twelve central quantities for findability, all resolve. PROJECTION compares all 48 headings field by field across source, bookmarks and typeset TOC.

Two things I'd flag rather than let pass as settled.

**Register 313 is the one worth reading.** My E(Λ_G) = 18 was a truncation artifact — I sliced the staircase mid-level. Localising it rather than just correcting it produced the third gap class in §13.2: **a partial survey reports E = 0 falsely if it stops on a level boundary.** That is a property of every incomplete pangenome, and it only exists in the paper because the mistake was investigated instead of fixed.

**The ledger is now five of six.** Adding gnomAD's constraint metrics and the four-gamete test, five of six components were already in print or already in the framework before I derived them. The protocol meant to prevent that has now failed at the same rate across three separate turns.

cell={c:(c[0],c[1],c[2]+c[3]*.26) for c in LG}

    ax.view_init(el,az);ax.set_title(t,fontsize=7.5,loc='left',pad=-2)

# The budget in motion

## E is not a stock

§6 partitions E by the modality of the admitted cell — forbidden, unknown, realisable — and treats
the partition as fixed. It is not. Evolution and sequencing both move cells between the three
classes, and the partition is a snapshot of a distribution mid-transit.

![The three modalities are one quantity in three states, with transitions between
them.](fig/f9_flow.pdf){width=100%}

forbidden: a cell absent despite full mutational opportunity is a cell the world forbids. **Drift and
fixation** move cells between forbidden and realisable as environments change. E measured at an
instant tells you the state of the flow, not a property of the index.

Among the living, any given site-alternate exists in **2Nμ ≈ 200 people**, taking N = 8 × 10⁹ and
μ = 1.25 × 10⁻⁸. But 807,162 individuals is **1.01 × 10⁻⁴** of that population. The two regimes are

| regime | an absent admitted cell means | status |
|---|---|---|
| sampling-limited | not enough people looked at | **here** |
| selection-limited | incompatible with life | not yet |

sample sizes in the millions to hundreds of millions will be required. **In the second regime E
becomes a direct measurement of lethality** — the contingent budget acquiring the coordinate budget's
modality through the passage of time.

`possible_variants` per trinucleotide context, which is E restricted to a functional class. It is the
fifth entry in the ledger of §17 and the closest of them: this paper's quantity under another name.

and that E should reproduce the classical four-gamete test. Tested exhaustively:

| m | four-gamete failures | E > 0 | sensitivity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 10 | 3 | 30.0% |
| 3 | 212 | 182 | 69.8% |
| 4 | 37,984 | 64,804 | 98.1% |

m ≤ 3.](fig/f10_fourgamete.pdf){width=100%}

chains — {00,01,11} and {00,10,11} have no incomparable pair, so no join is demanded and the missing
gamete is invisible to closure. The order evolution supplies is real and **too coarse for the
statistic population genetics already has.**

A related prediction also fell: that E on the mutational path lattice would isolate epistasis.
Threshold sets are up-sets, closed under join and not under meet, so additive landscapes break
closure on their own — mean E of 4.17 additive against 4.54 sign-epistatic, indistinguishable. The
signal exists but not on that lattice; §13 finds it on the right one.

# Dominance, and where ℛ runs in hardware

## The identification

A dominant allele is expressed as the maximum over the pair. A recessive trait appears only when both
alleles are recessive, which is the minimum. Ordering alleles recessive < dominant:

| genotype | dominant shows | join | recessive shows | meet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a,a) | a | a | a | a |
| (a,A) | A | A | a | a |
| (A,A) | A | A | A | A |

> **Dominance is the join. Recessivity is the meet.** Not an analogy — the same operation, verified
> on all four genotypes.

## Every classical mode closes

On the dosage chain k ∈ {0,1,2}, with phenotype as a function of dominant-allele count, §4's lemma
applies directly:

| mode | phenotype by k | monotone | E |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete dominant | 0, 1, 1 | yes | **0** |
| complete recessive | 0, 0, 1 | yes | **0** |
| additive / codominant | 0, 1, 2 | yes | **0** |
| partial dominance | 0, 2, 3 | yes | **0** |
| **overdominance** | 0, 2, 1 | no | **2** |
| **underdominance** | 2, 0, 2 | no | **2** |

![Every monotone dominance mode closes; only the heterozygote-extreme modes
open.](fig/f13_dominance.pdf){width=100%}

E there measures heterosis directly. The ABO series is also closed — A ∨ B = AB and A ∧ B = O are
both present — but at density 1.00, a full box, and by §2.2 it carries nothing.

## What E is blind to, and what it sees

A prediction of ours failed usefully: a recessive lethal does **not** break closure. At a single locus
*every* selection regime gives E = 0 — recessive lethal, dominant lethal, even the heterozygote
absent — because any subset of a three-element chain is still a chain. **E is completely blind to
single-locus selection.**

Two loci is where it bites:

| | genotypes | E |
|---|---|---|
| all viable | 9/9 | 0 |
| recessive lethal at locus 1 | 6/9 | **0** |
| recessive lethal at both loci | 4/9 | **0** |
| complementary lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| synthetic lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| heterozygote advantage only | 5/9 | **2** |

Independent effects at any number of loci leave E at zero. **E > 0 exactly when selection is
non-additive.**

## The one index that closes itself

Every other index in this paper requires someone to *apply* ℛ — a consortium sequencing centromeres,
a curator sorting chromosomes, an author re-running an audit. **Diploidy does not.** Join and meet are
computed at every locus of every cell continuously, as biochemistry, with no operator applied from
outside.

> **An open index does not close itself, except where the closure operator is realised in the object's
> own structure. Diploidy realises it. There the index genuinely closes itself, continuously and
> without agency, and what remains open after it has is exactly the non-additive part of selection.**

This suggests, and does not establish, that closure requires two copies: both operations are needed,
and a haploid genome has nothing to take a meet with. We have not tested it.

# Λ_G — the diploid genome lattice

## Construction

The new law supplies a bound the haploid indices never had, and it is Λ's own counting form:

$$\\Lambda_G = \\{(u,a,k,e) : a < A(u),\\; k \\le 2,\\; e \\le k\\}$$

| constraint | origin |
|---|---|
| a < A(u) | two haplotypes differing in a child snarl differ in its parent |
| k ≤ 2 | ploidy |
| **e ≤ k** | **cannot express more copies than are carried** |

All three are forced rather than assigned — the first index in this paper of which that is true.

| | |
|---|---|
| \\|Λ_G\\| at full scale | 3,756 cells (626 staircase × 6 triangle) |
| ambient box | 24,534 |
| **E(Λ_G)** | **0**, verified exhaustively at four staircase sizes |
| **density** | **0.1531** |

![Λ_G in four projections. Panel (d), viewed along u, collapses the staircase and shows the dosage
triangle e ≤ k — the new law in one shape.](fig/f14_lambdaG.pdf){width=100%}

Against the snarl tower alone at density 0.2296: **the diploid axes lower the density and keep the
zero, so by §2.2 the zero is stronger** — computed in a box 6.5 times its own size rather than 4.4.

## Three gap classes

**Copy number breaks the ploidy cap.** Raising k ≤ 2 to k ≤ P preserves closure at every P; triangles
of 6, 10 and 15 cells all give E = 0. But P is a per-locus capacity and loci are labelled by position:
a monotone P vector gives E = 0 and [2,4,2,3,2] gives **E = 5**. **CNV fails exactly the way (chr,pos)
failed in §3**, which is the paper's own defect recurring at its last coordinate.

**Epistasis is where Λ_G opens.** Two independent loci give 36 cells and E = 0, a product of closed
sets. Every interaction is a cell removal, and E counts them exactly.

![Λ_G is closed precisely because it contains no epistasis.](fig/f15_epistasis.pdf){width=100%}

**Truncation, and this class is dangerous.** A partial survey opens the index irregularly: truncating
a 17-cell staircase to 12 gives E = 3, to 8 gives E = 2, and to **10 gives E = 0** — because that cut
lands on a level boundary. **An incomplete survey can pass the closure test by accident.** E = 0
implies completeness only if you also know you stopped nowhere in particular.

## A weakness in the new bound

**e ≤ k cannot fail as defined here.** If e counts expressed *copies* the bound is definitional and
does no work. It acquires content only under the other reading — expressed *products* — where
alternative splicing makes one copy yield many transcripts and e > k directly. The constraint is
either forced-and-empty or contentful-and-false depending on which e is meant, and this paper takes
the first without having chosen. Register 313.

# The shape of the measurements

Turning the method on the paper's own results. Four axes carried the work: **bound origin** (assigned
by convention / forced by argument), **content locus** (in the bounds / in the selection among cells),
**label orientation** (ordered by capacity or not), and **temporality** (snapshot / process). Ten of
sixteen cells were measured.

![The measurement set. Two admitted-and-absent cells are definable; four lie outside ℛ
entirely.](fig/f11_shape.pdf){width=100%}

**E(session) = 2** at density 0.625. The non-trivial zero sits at exactly one corner — forced bound,
content in the bounds, label sorted, synchronic — where Λ, the snarl tower and Λ_G all live, which is
why they behave alike. The marginals give the shape: three axes balanced at 4–6 of 8, and

| | measured |
|---|---|
| synchronic | **8 / 8** |
| diachronic | **2 / 8** |

**The work is a snapshot with two process cells attached.**

The two admitted-and-absent cells are (0,1,1,1) and (1,1,1,1): *content in selection, ordered by
capacity, watched over time* — a **constraint map**, sites ranked by how much variation they can
carry, tracked as the sample grows. The two differ only in whether the bound is a fitted mutational
model or lethality itself, so **the gap is the transit between the regimes of §11.2.**

Four cells fall outside ℛ entirely, all with content in the bounds and diachronic: an index whose
*bounds themselves change over time* — genome size evolution, gene family expansion. Real objects
that the closure does not propose, because nothing measured lies adjacent.

> **A gap the closure admits is a prediction and has coordinates. A region the closure does not reach
> is an absence and has none.** Two definable, four not.

**The four axes are ours**, chosen by reading back over what the work turned on, and a different
choice gives a different E. Density 0.625 is high, so by §2.2 this near-closure is a weak result.

# The law

A law was proposed for this framework: *an open index is always trying to close itself.* It was tested
against every measurement in this paper with a nonzero E, over the intervals those indices have
existed.

![Larger E predicts less movement, not more.](fig/f12_law.pdf){width=100%}

| index | E | interval | moved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| assembly gaps | 150,630,700 | 2013 → 2022 | **yes, to zero** |
| audit defects | 3 | four runs | **yes, to zero** |
| variant occupancy | 9,264,809,496 | 2016 → 2024 | **yes, 8.49% and rising** |
| chromosome (chr,pos) | 2,886,684,296 | 2009 → now | **no** |
| snarl orientation | 2,100 | 2018 → now | no |
| genome sequence | 9,264,809,496 | ever | no, and must not |
| pangenome alleles | 12 | 2023 → now | no |

available and unexecuted across two reference builds and seventeen years. Neither E nor the external
description length predicts movement — larger E predicts *less*. What predicts it, in all seven cases,
is whether closing serves what the index is *for*.

> **An index does not close itself; it states what closing would cost. Closure follows alignment with
> purpose, not the size of E. And ℛ, applied regardless, will close either one and certify both.**

The second clause is §3.3 restated as law. The danger is not indices that stay open; it is indices
that close wrongly and pass their own audit.

**Alignment is a label assigned after the outcomes were known** — seven cases, a binary of our
choosing, and it cannot yet fail. It becomes a law only applied forward, so: the pangenome allele
index will *not* be reordered by carrier count however large its E grows, and the constraint-map gap
of §14 *will* close, because closing it is what sequencing more people does. If the first closes or
the second stalls, the law is wrong.

"""

![E is neither sound nor complete against the four-gamete test — 34 soundness counterexamples at
m ≤ 3.](fig/f10_fourgamete.pdf){width=100%}

**Neither sound nor complete.** The two three-haplotype sets E misses at m = 2 are exactly the
chains — {00,01,11} and {00,10,11} have no incomparable pair, so no join is demanded and the missing
gamete is invisible to closure. The order evolution supplies is real and **too coarse for the
statistic population genetics already has.**

A related prediction also fell: that E on the mutational path lattice would isolate epistasis.
Threshold sets are up-sets, closed under join and not under meet, so additive landscapes break
closure on their own — mean E of 4.17 additive against 4.54 sign-epistatic, indistinguishable. The
signal exists but not on that lattice; §13 finds it on the right one.

# Dominance, and where ℛ runs in hardware

## The identification

A dominant allele is expressed as the maximum over the pair. A recessive trait appears only when both
alleles are recessive, which is the minimum. Ordering alleles recessive < dominant:

| genotype | dominant shows | join | recessive shows | meet |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a,a) | a | a | a | a |
| (a,A) | A | A | a | a |
| (A,A) | A | A | A | A |

> **Dominance is the join. Recessivity is the meet.** Not an analogy — the same operation, verified
> on all four genotypes.

## Every classical mode closes

On the dosage chain k ∈ {0,1,2}, with phenotype as a function of dominant-allele count, §4's lemma
applies directly:

| mode | phenotype by k | monotone | E |
|---|---|---|---|
| complete dominant | 0, 1, 1 | yes | **0** |
| complete recessive | 0, 0, 1 | yes | **0** |
| additive / codominant | 0, 1, 2 | yes | **0** |
| partial dominance | 0, 2, 3 | yes | **0** |
| **overdominance** | 0, 2, 1 | no | **2** |
| **underdominance** | 2, 0, 2 | no | **2** |

![Every monotone dominance mode closes; only the heterozygote-extreme modes
open.](fig/f13_dominance.pdf){width=100%}

E there measures heterosis directly. The ABO series is also closed — A ∨ B = AB and A ∧ B = O are
both present — but at density 1.00, a full box, and by §2.2 it carries nothing.

## What E is blind to, and what it sees

A prediction of ours failed usefully: a recessive lethal does **not** break closure. At a single locus
*every* selection regime gives E = 0 — recessive lethal, dominant lethal, even the heterozygote
absent — because any subset of a three-element chain is still a chain. **E is completely blind to
single-locus selection.**

Two loci is where it bites:

| | genotypes | E |
|---|---|---|
| all viable | 9/9 | 0 |
| recessive lethal at locus 1 | 6/9 | **0** |
| recessive lethal at both loci | 4/9 | **0** |
| complementary lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| synthetic lethal | 8/9 | **1** |
| heterozygote advantage only | 5/9 | **2** |

Independent effects at any number of loci leave E at zero. **E > 0 exactly when selection is
non-additive.**

## The one index that closes itself

Every other index in this paper requires someone to *apply* ℛ — a consortium sequencing centromeres,
a curator sorting chromosomes, an author re-running an audit. **Diploidy does not.** Join and meet are
computed at every locus of every cell continuously, as biochemistry, with no operator applied from
outside.

> **An open index does not close itself, except where the closure operator is realised in the object's
> own structure. Diploidy realises it. There the index genuinely closes itself, continuously and
> without agency, and what remains open after it has is exactly the non-additive part of selection.**

This suggests, and does not establish, that closure requires two copies: both operations are needed,
and a haploid genome has nothing to take a meet with. We have not tested it.

# Λ_G — the diploid genome lattice

## Construction

The new law supplies a bound the haploid indices never had, and it is Λ's own counting form:

$$\\Lambda_G = \\{(u,a,k,e) : a < A(u),\\; k \\le 2,\\; e \\le k\\}$$

| constraint | origin |
|---|---|
| a < A(u) | two haplotypes differing in a child snarl differ in its parent |
| k ≤ 2 | ploidy |
| **e ≤ k** | **cannot express more copies than are carried** |

All three are forced rather than assigned — the first index in this paper of which that is true.

| | |
|---|---|
| \\|Λ_G\\| at full scale | 3,756 cells (626 staircase × 6 triangle) |
| ambient box | 24,534 |
| **E(Λ_G)** | **0**, verified exhaustively at four staircase sizes |
| **density** | **0.1531** |

![Λ_G in four projections. Panel (d), viewed along u, collapses the staircase and shows the dosage
triangle e ≤ k — the new law in one shape.](fig/f14_lambdaG.pdf){width=100%}

Against the snarl tower alone at density 0.2296: **the diploid axes lower the density and keep the
zero, so by §2.2 the zero is stronger** — computed in a box 6.5 times its own size rather than 4.4.

## Three gap classes

**Copy number breaks the ploidy cap.** Raising k ≤ 2 to k ≤ P preserves closure at every P; triangles
of 6, 10 and 15 cells all give E = 0. But P is a per-locus capacity and loci are labelled by position:
a monotone P vector gives E = 0 and [2,4,2,3,2] gives **E = 5**. **CNV fails exactly the way (chr,pos)
failed in §3**, which is the paper's own defect recurring at its last coordinate.

**Epistasis is where Λ_G opens.** Two independent loci give 36 cells and E = 0, a product of closed
sets. Every interaction is a cell removal, and E counts them exactly.

![Λ_G is closed precisely because it contains no epistasis.](fig/f15_epistasis.pdf){width=100%}

**Truncation, and this class is dangerous.** A partial survey opens the index irregularly: truncating
a 17-cell staircase to 12 gives E = 3, to 8 gives E = 2, and to **10 gives E = 0** — because that cut
lands on a level boundary. **An incomplete survey can pass the closure test by accident.** E = 0
implies completeness only if you also know you stopped nowhere in particular.

## A weakness in the new bound

**e ≤ k cannot fail as defined here.** If e counts expressed *copies* the bound is definitional and
does no work. It acquires content only under the other reading — expressed *products* — where
alternative splicing makes one copy yield many transcripts and e > k directly. The constraint is
either forced-and-empty or contentful-and-false depending on which e is meant, and this paper takes
the first without having chosen. Register 313.

# The shape of the measurements

Turning the method on the paper's own results. Four axes carried the work: **bound origin** (assigned
by convention / forced by argument), **content locus** (in the bounds / in the selection among cells),
**label orientation** (ordered by capacity or not), and **temporality** (snapshot / process). Ten of
sixteen cells were measured.

![The measurement set. Two admitted-and-absent cells are definable; four lie outside ℛ
entirely.](fig/f11_shape.pdf){width=100%}

**E(session) = 2** at density 0.625. The non-trivial zero sits at exactly one corner — forced bound,
content in the bounds, label sorted, synchronic — where Λ, the snarl tower and Λ_G all live, which is
why they behave alike. The marginals give the shape: three axes balanced at 4–6 of 8, and

| | measured |
|---|---|
| synchronic | **8 / 8** |
| diachronic | **2 / 8** |

**The work is a snapshot with two process cells attached.**

The two admitted-and-absent cells are (0,1,1,1) and (1,1,1,1): *content in selection, ordered by
capacity, watched over time* — a **constraint map**, sites ranked by how much variation they can
carry, tracked as the sample grows. The two differ only in whether the bound is a fitted mutational
model or lethality itself, so **the gap is the transit between the regimes of §11.2.**

Four cells fall outside ℛ entirely, all with content in the bounds and diachronic: an index whose
*bounds themselves change over time* — genome size evolution, gene family expansion. Real objects
that the closure does not propose, because nothing measured lies adjacent.

> **A gap the closure admits is a prediction and has coordinates. A region the closure does not reach
> is an absence and has none.** Two definable, four not.

**The four axes are ours**, chosen by reading back over what the work turned on, and a different
choice gives a different E. Density 0.625 is high, so by §2.2 this near-closure is a weak result.

# The law

A law was proposed for this framework: *an open index is always trying to close itself.* It was tested
against every measurement in this paper with a nonzero E, over the intervals those indices have
existed.

![Larger E predicts less movement, not more.](fig/f12_law.pdf){width=100%}

| index | E | interval | moved? |
|---|---|---|---|
| assembly gaps | 150,630,700 | 2013 → 2022 | **yes, to zero** |
| audit defects | 3 | four runs | **yes, to zero** |
| variant occupancy | 9,264,809,496 | 2016 → 2024 | **yes, 8.49% and rising** |
| chromosome (chr,pos) | 2,886,684,296 | 2009 → now | **no** |
| snarl orientation | 2,100 | 2018 → now | no |
| genome sequence | 9,264,809,496 | ever | no, and must not |
| pangenome alleles | 12 | 2023 → now | no |

**The law fails four of seven.** The chromosome index decides it: E = 2.89 × 10⁹, a costless repair,
available and unexecuted across two reference builds and seventeen years. Neither E nor the external
description length predicts movement — larger E predicts *less*. What predicts it, in all seven cases,
is whether closing serves what the index is *for*.

> **An index does not close itself; it states what closing would cost. Closure follows alignment with
> purpose, not the size of E. And ℛ, applied regardless, will close either one and certify both.**

The second clause is §3.3 restated as law. The danger is not indices that stay open; it is indices
that close wrongly and pass their own audit.

**Alignment is a label assigned after the outcomes were known** — seven cases, a binary of our
choosing, and it cannot yet fail. It becomes a law only applied forward, so: the pangenome allele
index will *not* be reordered by carrier count however large its E grows, and the constraint-map gap
of §14 *will* close, because closing it is what sequencing more people does. If the first closes or
the second stalls, the law is wrong.

"""

**312.** §9 described the 8.49% occupancy as the contingent budget being spent. It is a **sampling**

content.text:
Caught up. **31 pages, 19 sections, 15 figures, 17 registers, 10,132 extractable words. 20 PASS, 0 FLAG, 0 FAIL.**

**Five sections added:** §11 The budget in motion (E as flow, the two regimes, the four-gamete negative), §12 Dominance, and where ℛ runs in hardware, §13 Λ_G — the diploid genome lattice, §14 The shape of the measurements, §15 The law. Seven new figures, all generated from the computations they depict.

**Two corrections to sections already in the delivered PDF**, which matter more than the additions:

- **§5's triangulated law is now bounded to synchronic indices.** It was stated unrestricted. Evolution supplies labels that are not conventional — ancestral versus derived is fixed by outgroup comparison — so the law as printed was an overreach. Register 311.
- **§9's 8.49% is relabelled a sampling readout, not the budget being spent.** 807,162 individuals is 1.01 × 10⁻⁴ of the living population. Register 312.

**One real audit failure, on MEASURE.** Fifteen figures referenced, fifteen files on disk, and a generation record still asserting eight — written by the first figure pass and never revised. Register 306's class exactly: a statement agreeing with a version of the work that no longer exists. Repaired at the record, not the detector, because an audit adjusted to match the artefact it disagrees with has been disabled rather than satisfied. Register 314.

The audits now carry thirteen equations and ten arithmetic checks, including the new lattice: Λ_G density 0.1531, |Λ_G| = 3,756, the dosage triangle closing at E = 0, overdominance at E = 2, and the two-locus product closing. ARTEFACT probes twelve central quantities for findability, all resolve. PROJECTION compares all 48 headings field by field across source, bookmarks and typeset TOC.

Two things I'd flag rather than let pass as settled.

**Register 313 is the one worth reading.** My E(Λ_G) = 18 was a truncation artifact — I sliced the staircase mid-level. Localising it rather than just correcting it produced the third gap class in §13.2: **a partial survey reports E = 0 falsely if it stops on a level boundary.** That is a property of every incomplete pangenome, and it only exists in the paper because the mistake was investigated instead of fixed.

**The ledger is now five of six.** Adding gnomAD's constraint metrics and the four-gamete test, five of six components were already in print or already in the framework before I derived them. The protocol meant to prevent that has now failed at the same rate across three separate turns.
